notes: runtime_s covers composite() only (input already in RAM); load_s is the npz read.
peak_mem_mb_composite is tracemalloc peak during composite(), excluding the input array (see input_array_mb).

median_year sorts in uint16 with a 65535 sentinel and counts valid obs from the mask (65535 is also a real saturated DN in the data); self_test checks it equals an np.nanmedian float32 oracle exactly.
Even clear counts average the two middle values, so the composite pixel can be a value no real date had; bands may also come from different dates.
Reflectance DN 0 is treated as fill in addition to the QA rule; valid medians are clipped to >= 1 to keep 0 = nodata.
nodata_pixel_frac = fraction of pixels with no clear observation, averaged over years.

Timings were taken while the other S2 spike agents ran in parallel on the same machine; an isolated one-year benchmark took ~0.06 s/year (~2.6 s/place at N=4), so these numbers are likely pessimistic.
Peak memory is dominated by the output array (43 years x 6 x 334 x 334 uint16 = 55 MB); per-year working set is ~10 MB at N=6.

Surprise: reflectance DN 65535 appears in QA-clear pixels (saturation; QA_RADSAT is not part of the agreed mask). The median keeps them as valid; it tolerates a few, but a single-scene pick would not.
problems: First version used np.nanmedian: 12-19 s per place (masked-array fallback for short axes), over the 10 s budget. A float32 sort-based median got ~8-11 s; the uint16 sort version is used instead.
